method: BRANCH (feature red | regression red | proof review) x ARRIVAL (explicit | implicit | contextual). Positives cover the three branches and all arrival styles; negatives are adjacent testing jobs where red_check cannot judge the result.

cases.prompt: Use tdd-dev for the first acceptance criterion of this approved feature before you write production code.
We have three acceptance criteria and no code yet. Drive the first vertical slice test-first, prove its red, and run the relevant regression suite before moving on.
The API plan is approved. Start with the public CLI contract, not the parser internals, and prove the missing behaviour before implementing it.
Run tdd-dev: the fix already exists, but I need evidence that the regression test catches the old defect and the relevant suite remains green.
This test is green after my patch. Show that it fails when the bug is safely reintroduced, then verify the repaired tree.
The PR is ready and tests pass, but none of the new tests was ever observed failing. Close that evidence gap without touching unrelated dirty work.
Does this passing parser test prove the contract, or is it mirroring the same branches and fixtures as the implementation?
Before calling the bug done, inspect the recorded red reason and reject it if the failure was only a missing fixture or environment error.
Build a load test and define the p95 latency budget for this endpoint.
The upstream SDK crashes internally and we cannot reproduce it in our code; document a pinned workaround and upstream issue.
Review this existing test suite for naming consistency and duplicated fixtures; do not change product behaviour.
Add a production health probe for the queue and alert when no jobs complete for ten minutes.
